title: A skyscraper sheaf of sets at a point is the direct image of the constant sheaf on the closure of the point
statement:
Let $Y$ be a topological space, $y\in Y$, $W=\overline{\{y\}}$ the closure of $\{y\}$ with inclusion $i_W:W	o Y$, and $A$ a set. Let $i_{y,*}A$ be the skyscraper sheaf at $y$ with value $A$: the sheaf of sets on $Y$ with $(i_{y,*}A)(V)=A$ if $y\in V$ and $(i_{y,*}A)(V)=\{*\}$ (a one-point set) if $y
otin V$ ($V\subseteq Y$ open), the restriction maps being the identity of $A$ when the smaller open contains $y$ and the map to $\{*\}$ otherwise. Let $(i_W)_*\underline A_W$ be the sheaf of sets $V\mapsto\{$locally constant maps $V\cap W	o A\}$ on $Y$ (restriction of maps as restriction maps). Then: (1) for every open $V\subseteq Y$, $V\cap W
eq\emptyset$ if and only if $y\in V$; (2) if $y\in V$, every locally constant map $V\cap W	o A$ is constant; (3) consequently the maps $\kappa_V:(i_{y,*}A)(V)	o(i_W)_*\underline A_W(V)$, sending $a\in A$ to the constant map with value $a$ when $y\in V$, and $*$ to the empty map when $y
otin V$, are bijective and form an isomorphism of sheaves of sets $\kappa:i_{y,*}A\xrightarrow{\sim}(i_W)_*\underline A_W$.
